outcomes.original: Filing step: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain an Employer Identification Number from the IRS, then register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to receive a Business Account Number. What to say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online at bizfile.sos.ca.gov. Within 90 days, file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an EIN at irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/apply-for-an-employer-identification-number-ein-online (free, issued immediately). With the EIN and entity documents, register online with the SF Treasurer at sftreasurer.org/business/register-your-business; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (for example, $55 up to $100k, each plus a $4 state fee). The Business Account Number is required for every other city permit.

outcomes.original: Filing step: While the CUA is under review, engage a California ABC license broker to identify available Type 48 licenses for sale and transfer to 270 Columbus Ave, and request a quote with escrow timeline. What to say: Contact a licensed ABC license broker (search the California ABC website for brokers active in San Francisco County). Explain that you need a Type 48 on-sale general public premises license transferred to 270 Columbus Ave, San Francisco 94133, census tract 106.00. Ask for available licenses, current asking prices (expect $100,000–$450,000), escrow and transfer timelines (typically 90–180 days including ABC posting and local sign-off), and whether the broker can assist with the Public Convenience or Necessity finding if the tract is over-concentrated. Do not enter escrow or pay a deposit until the CUA is approved and the lease is signed with a contingency allowing you to cancel if the ABC transfer is denied.
outcomes.note: Records show license cost $17,000-$450,000 (not $100,000-$450,000) and timeline 120-300 days (not 90-180 days); census tract number and over-concentration status not stated.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the Planning Commission approves the CUA, obtain a California Seller's Permit from CDTFA and file the ABC license transfer application (person-to-person and premises-to-premises) with the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control. What to say: Register online at onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov (free, often issued same day). With the seller's permit, the signed lease, the approved CUA, and the Business Account Number, complete ABC Form ABC-257 (application for transfer of license) and pay the ABC fee (roughly $1,000–$1,600). ABC will post a notice at 270 Columbus for 30 days and send the application to SFPD and Planning for review. If census tract 106.00 is over-concentrated (52 licenses against 12 authorized), request a Public Convenience or Necessity determination from the San Francisco Board of Supervisors or Planning Department (the process varies by jurisdiction); the broker or ABC district office can explain the local PCN procedure. Budget 90–180 days for the transfer if unprotested, or 4–6 months if a PCN hearing is required.
outcomes.note: Records show seller's permit is free and often same-day, but do not state the website URL, ABC form number, specific procedures, census tract details, or timelines; ABC fee in records is $17,000–$450,000, not $1,000–$1,600; timeline is 120–300 days.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Apply for the San Francisco Department of Public Health Permit to Operate a food facility, submitting the menu, equipment list, and layout drawings online at least one month before the planned opening. What to say: Log in to the DPH Environmental Health portal at sfdph.org/dph/EH/Food and create an account with your Business Account Number, Location ID, and EIN. Upload the menu (limited-kitchen food), a scaled floor plan showing the kitchen, bar, hand sinks, three-compartment sink, and restrooms, and an equipment list. One owner or employee must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety manager certification exam (ServSafe or equivalent, about $125–$200) within 60 days of opening; upload the certificate with the application. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (includes initial inspection). DPH will review the plans (14–60 days) and schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% completion and a final inspection before issuing the permit. Do not serve the public before the permit is issued.

outcomes.original: Filing step: If tenant improvements are needed (kitchen build-out, ADA upgrades, accessibility), file a building permit application with the Department of Building Inspection, routed to Planning for change-of-use review. What to say: Hire an architect licensed in California to prepare a set of plans stamped for the work (kitchen equipment, plumbing, electrical, mechanical, ADA path of travel). Submit the building permit application at sfdbi.org/permit-applications, checking the 'change of use' box and attaching the approved CUA. DBI will route the application to Planning, DPH (plan check), SFFD (if a commercial hood is installed or occupant load is 50+), and SFPUC (for a grease interceptor if cooking). Pay the permit fee (a percentage of construction valuation, typically $800–$15,000 depending on scope). Licensed subcontractors will pull separate electrical, plumbing, and mechanical permits. Schedule the DPH pre-final inspection, the DBI and SFFD final inspections, and the DPH final health inspection in that order, booking each at least two weeks in advance.
outcomes.note: The records mention grease interceptor requirements and health permit inspections but do not state the building permit filing procedures, routing, fees, architect requirements, or inspection sequences described.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 134 to 360 days. Estimated government cost: $20,775 to $467,400. Notes: The timeline and cost cover the Conditional Use Authorization, the ABC Type 48 license transfer, the health permit, and the building permit with change-of-use review, assuming all are approved. The day range (134–360 days) is the time from filing the CUA to obtaining all approvals when they are granted: CUA 120–300 days, ABC transfer (if unprotested in an over-concentrated tract with PCN review) 90–180 days overlapping with the CUA, health permit 14–45 days, and building permit (if needed) 14–120 days. The CUA and ABC transfer run in parallel after the CUA is approved, so the longer of the two sets the critical path. The cost range ($20,775–$467,400) includes CUA application fee $3,100–$15,000, ABC license purchase and transfer $17,000–$450,000 (the license itself, not a government fee, dominates the range), health permit $470–$1,000, building permit $800–$15,000 if tenant improvements are needed, business registration $55–$700, entity formation $70–$150, and seller's permit $0. It does not include construction costs, rent, or operating expenses. The timeline assumes approval; a CUA denial, a withdrawn application, or an ABC transfer denial would end the process without opening, and no time to a denial or withdrawal is estimated here. Confirm the formula retail status and obtain a written zoning determination from Planning before beginning the ABC license search, because if a CUA is not required the timeline shortens by 4–10 months and the cost drops by $3,000–$15,000.
